articles.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
articles.summary: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer. As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show.
body: Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show.

articles.title: PS5’s Exciting New Zelda-Like Kena Game Just Got Delayed
articles.summary: Developer Ember Lab has announced that its upcoming PS5 game Kena: Scars of Kosmora, the sequel to 2021's much-loved Kena: Bridge of Spirits, has been delayed. The game-- which gives off major Zelda vibes --was previously set to release this year, but now it's been delayed to 2027.
body: In a blog post, the developers said they need more time to "deliver a top-notch game that exceeds the quality" of Bridge of Spirits. "Pushing our release into 2027 gives us the ability to really polish the expanded game experience we want to deliver," the studio said.
Scars of Kosmora is a linear adventure game, just like the 2021 entry, but the sequel has a "broader and deeper scope," the studio said.

"We hope you’re just as excited to jump into Kena’s next adventure as we are to share it with you. We’ve been working hard to fill it with the wonder, charm, and challenge fans have come to expect," the team added. "We appreciate your patience and support as we take the time for Scars of Kosmora to be the evolution of Kena’s journey and experience we want to deliver."

In Scars of Kosmora, main character Kena is now a seasoned spirit guide and embarks on a journey to the island of Kosmora to find a "cure for her affliction and to reconnect with a friend from her past." The island holds a "powerful corruption" that fractures her staff, so Kena adopts a new method of manipulating the elements to her advantage.

articles.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
articles.summary: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
body: If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God.

The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.”

I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice.

articles.title: Lanterns Rakes In More Than 18 Million Views Per Episode Globally As Season Finale Approaches
articles.summary: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.
body: As shared by Variety, statistics compiled by media research firm Nielsen show that Lanterns’ seventh episode accrued seven million views within the United States during its first three days, combined across HBO’s cable channels and its streaming service, HBO Max.

In the US, Lanterns is reportedly averaging more than 12 million views per episode; that number increases to 19 million when taking global viewership into account. Variety notes that it’s highly likely these numbers will continue to rise, as 1.5 million new viewers reportedly watched Lanterns’ premier episode just last week.

With these latest stats in mind, Lanterns is rubbing elbows with other uber-popular HBO releases; DC’s previous series on the streamer, The Penguin, averaged 27 million views per episode back in 2024, while shows like Euphoria averaged 25 million per episode by the end of its third and final season. Award-winning medical drama The Pitt averaged 15.4 million views on Season 2, the finale of which garnered 9.7 million views.

articles.title: 'Digger' Ending Explained: A Spoiler-Filled Breakdown of Tom Cruise's Wild New Movie
articles.summary: Digger contains three big reveals that reshape our understanding of the movie in various ways. To really understand what Digger is about, you need to grapple with all three, and the way they fit together (both successfully and unsuccessfully) to tell a complex story about finding meaning at the end…
body: Digger is many things. It’s the first Tom Cruise movie in over a decade not to feature recognizable IP, fighter planes, or both. Its director Alejandro Iñárritu's biggest swing yet after divisive, high-brow films like Birdman and The Revenant. It’s a brutal condemnation of late-stage capitalism. It’s also a pretty clever magic trick.

The first big reveal comes about 30 minutes into Digger. After meeting the aging oil baron Rockwell Digger (Cruise), we quickly learn that his Greenland drilling operation has accidentally dislodged a massive hunk of ice into the Atlantic Ocean, and it’s heading straight for Northern Europe. The U.S. President (John Goodman) and his cabinet show up at Digger’s mansion to discuss their best options (there are none). Then, as Digger and President Compson step aside into a private room to discuss other matters, Iñárritu plays his first trick: The majestic tree outside slowly tips over in front of them… and then a giant hand reaches out from behind the horizon to grab it.
points: Digger contains three big reveals that reshape our understanding of the movie in various ways.
It’s the first Tom Cruise movie in over a decade not to feature recognizable IP, fighter planes, or both.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Weather System Sounds Like A Big Step Up
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 includes a number of updates and improvements over the developer's past games, and that includes new weather systems. Rockstar's vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar, Owen Shepherd, told Game Informer that the studio has "re-engineered" the…
body: He said the goal was to make the weather in GTA 6's setting of Leonida--a stand-in for Florida--feel "dynamically solid and achieve a sense of scale" that the studio has never done before.
What that means in practice is that GTA 6 will have "fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map" to provide a "broad spectrum of weather" in the game.

Florida is known for its heat and humidity, along with its localized and fast-moving rain systems. Look one direction and you may see bright sunshine. Look the other and you could see a downpour. GTA 6 will replicate this with localized rain showers, along with rainbows that appear. Additionally, places where it recently rained in the game will remain wet, with puddles also popping up.

GTA 6 also has a new wind system that includes "offshore breezes after sunset, convectional updrafts, and occlusion from buildings,” Shepherd said. “Hair and debris will swirl around on rooftops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps.”

articles.title: 'Verity' Ending Explained: How That Bonkers Final Twist Reshapes the Entire Movie
articles.summary: Directed by Michael Showalter and based on one of Colleen Hoover’s most polarizing novels, Verity is a new movie that's just hit theaters, starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett.
body: The story follows Lowen Ashleigh (Johnson), a struggling writer who gets the opportunity of a lifetime when Jeremy Crawford (Hartnett), the husband of famous author Verity Crawford (Hathaway), offers her the chance to complete Verity’s successful book series.

The offer includes a huge sum of money and new living arrangements in the Crawfords’ stunning, remote Vermont mansion. As the film unfolds, Lowen and Jeremy fall in love, while Verity, paralyzed after a car crash, lives in the same home.

While working on the book, Lowen finds a hidden manuscript in Verity’s office. The text reveals Verity’s darkest secrets, including the fact that she finds no joy in motherhood and resents her twin children, Harper and Crew.
The most shocking part of the manuscript is the revelation that Verity orchestrated the boating accident that resulted in her daughter’s death.

articles.title: Blizzard Isn’t Fixing Diablo 4 Season 15’s Biggest Bug
articles.summary: Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced.
body: Hellfire Torch is a new Unique charm that counts as an extra set charm and comes with some great beneficial stats, like +All Skills, +All Stats, and +All Resistances. Players can usually only have one Unique charm equipped at a time, but Hellfire Torch breaks that rule, allowing players to use it and another Unique charm.

That's strong on its own, but there is currently a bugged interaction with Hellfire Torch that is allowing players to equip two Unique charms in addition to Hellfire Torch instead of one, granting even higher levels of power.

The bug seems to stem from Hellfire Torch being used first alongside the Seal of the Golden Epiphany, which allows players to equip up to three Unique charms. However, players are later swapping out Golden Epiphany for the Mythic Seal of the Diamond Mind, a seal that reduces the number of charms needed for set bonuses, but are still able to benefit from having additional Unique charms equipped. That, in turn, allows players to gain advantages from a full five-piece set bonus, Hellfire Torch, and two Unique charms all at once.
points: Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is 100x More Fun Playing Co-op
articles.summary: Playing solo, Gears of War: E-Day is a perfectly serviceable third-person shooter. Playing with a friend? On the same screen? Gears of War: E-Day is transcendent.
body: This is largely due to the modern gaming landscape, which has seen couch co-op games become as fleetingly rare as other once-common aspects of daily life, like Cava bowls and reading comprehension. Gears of War set the standard for local co-op back in the 2000s. During the Xbox 360 era, couch co-op games were everywhere. Even Insomniac made one. But due to a wide range of factors — shifting player tastes, technological restrictions, balance sheets — developers moved away from the trend. In 2026, Gears of War: E-Day stands out for offering a mode that’s more than just perfunctory. It’s essential.

“Splitscreen, specifically on console, that's core to Gears,” Gears of War brand director Nicole Fawcette told me during an interview at Gamescom 2026. “That's always been the DNA of the game. Like we are… We’ve always been a co-op game.”

articles.title: 5 Classic 'Unfilmable' Books That Should Never Get Adapted Into Movies
articles.summary: That said, some classic books should never be turned into films. This has less to do with their “unfilmable” nature. Some stories simply lose their essence as soon as they’re translated to another medium.
body: Some literary classics have managed to beat the “unadaptable” curse. Frank Herbert’s Dune is a key example, along with Stanisław Lem’s Solaris and Gabriel García Márquez’s One Hundred Years of Solitude. “If it can be written, or thought, it can be filmed,” said director Stanley Kubrick — a statement that has proven to be true in the hands of competent filmmakers.
With that in mind, here are five classic books that should never be adapted into movies.

Mark Z. Danielewski works with a metanarrative in his subversive House of Leaves, a tactile reading experience that cannot be replicated on film. The book doubles as an academic text about a fictional documentary film known as The Navidson Record, with the manuscript being edited by a man named Johnny Truant. This manuscript is filled with footnotes and anecdotes from Truant himself, some containing text that needs to be rotated to be read. House of Leaves uses convoluted layouts and chaotic formatting to tell its layered story. Some pages sport only a single word, while others feature messy overlaps to the point of being unreadable.
points: That said, some classic books should never be turned into films.
This has less to do with their “unfilmable” nature.

articles.title: PS5 Just Got A PS5 Pro-Like AI Upgrade, But Don’t Expect It Everywhere Yet
articles.summary: The base PS5 console is no slouch when it comes to games, but compared to the PS5 Pro, it doesn't pack the same visual punch. That could change soon, as Sony has unveiled a new AI-upscaling upgrade for the older machine called Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR).
body: "QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan's epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel's Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5," head of technology at Insomniac Games, Mike Fitzgerald, wrote in a PS Blog post.

Jasmin Patry, lead rendering engineer at Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch Productions, added that QSSR excels at "resolving the fine details" in characters and environments that previously wasn't possible on the base PS5. Both PS5 exclusives are receiving a patch today to add QSSR as an additional graphics option, and Sony says it will be offered to all PlayStation developers soon.

articles.summary: It's been a while since I set foot nervously inside the Playtime Co. factory, but last time I was there I was hounded through the halls and air vents by a towering blue plush toy that wanted nothing more than to hug me to death.
body: I played a bit of the multiplayer prequel to Poppy Playtime this week, and I can now report that there's something even scarier than that giant Huggy Wuggy doll roaming the factory. Her name is Miss Delight. You can meet her yourself because the Escape from Playtime open beta is now live on Steam and you can try out the game all weekend long.

This time you're one of the cute little Playtime toys, like a plush bunny, a cartoony cat, or a fluffy unicorn, and your goal is to escape the accursed factory with your pals by skittering through the dark corridors and shadowy rooms collecting supplies. Fill a cart with enough useful junk and you can advance to the next shift. Complete all the shifts and you're free. But it's not gonna be easy.

articles.title: Aion 2's imminent worldwide release could be huge as early access founders' packs outsell major games, and player numbers soar
articles.summary: Aion 2's much-awaited worldwide release is days away, following its release in Korea and Taiwan roughly a year ago. Despite this, the MMO has soared - high up Steam's most played game chart.
body: There are two charts that tell a story. The first is Aion 2 hitting the number-one spot on Steam's Top Sellers list. While Aion 2 is generally a free-to-play game, you currently have to buy your way into early access via a one of a few founders' packs. The cheapest of these packs is £18.49 and it comes with a stack of in-game cosmetics and consumables.

It's through these founders' packs that Aion has outsold other major recent releases. By revenue, Aion 2's founders' packs have made more than EA FC 27, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, and Gears of War: E-Day this week.

As for how many players are actually jumping into Aion 2 early, the Steam Most Played figures paint an interesting picture. As of writing, the game sits at the number nine spot, above Delta Force and Delta Lock, but not quite pushing past big-hitters like PUBG, Apex Legends, and recent multiplayer sensation Wardogs.

This is already an impressive position to be in, but it's of course expected to climb the ranks further once the game becomes open to non-founders a few days from now - and as it becomes free to play.

videos.summary: Ghost of Yotei's Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted DLC, reviewed by Michael Higham on PlayStation 5.
body: "This wave of paid DLC for Ghost of Yotei is a great reminder of just how graceful and deadly its combat can be, especially with how it's further emphasized in the new run-based Most Wanted mode. I didn't expect to get the itch for another run each time I was struck down, but that speaks to Yotei’s satisfying swordplay and the way these remixed challenges pushed me to think harder about every tool available. Echoes of Sekigahara isn't groundbreaking as an extension of the existing story, but Atsu gets a brief moment to shine again and show a more vulnerable, intimate side alongside a charming foil from her past. The battles within are familiar and the views are still impressive, but this one-two punch is a reminder of how fundamentally great Sucker Punch's ronin fantasy has been, and a layup for anyone looking for an excuse to return to Ghost of Yotei."
